cases.synthetic_source: Before sunrise, the harbor siren sounded once and went quiet.
Elena folded the map. At the gate, she handed it to Tomas.
Marcus locked the cabinet. Later, he checked it again.
Leah described the lantern falling. Omar later recalled the same fall from the doorway, while the fire that followed was separate.
Nora described the tower's collapse. Later, Eli spoke of the structure giving way at noon; both accounts concern one incident.
Cal opens the station. The narration then returns to the summer when his mother gave him the brass key.
The courier might have reached town before the blackout, or only after the generators restarted; no one can establish which.
Mira studies the tide chart because she wants to reach the island before dark. The gulls circle above her, but nothing says her studying caused them to circle.
Dane studies the tide table all afternoon. At sunset he leaves for the island, carrying only the route he memorized.
From Niko's viewpoint, the porch light seems to pulse. He believes Mara is awake, but he does not know whether anyone is inside.
The narration enters Ava's worry, then Ben's private relief, without settling on either mind as the permanent center.
The corridor again. Of course they had left Oren to discover the locked door alone; the thought tightened his chest.
Rosa tucks the blue ticket into her sleeve; the gesture plants an object for later and reveals how carefully she hides her fear.
A tiny scratch appears on the compass. Much later, the scratch bends the needle during the crossing, while the origin of a sealed note remains unanswered.
A cracked watch stops at 4:12. Much later, its frozen hands reveal when the power failed.
Tarin rejects the family bargain, but the story ends before showing whether his sister will forgive him.
At first, a silver ribbon marks a promise. Near the end, the same ribbon returns tied around a locked box, transforming the motif from promise to restraint.
